t: A tiny RISC-V chip with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth for very little money.
steps: Buy a Pine64 PineCone from the Pine64 store, or an Ai-Thinker Ai-WB2-32S-Kit from RobotShop.
Get a USB-C cable. Some e-marked cables fail to power the PineCone.
Install the Bouffalo bl_iot_sdk and its RISC-V GCC toolchain on your computer.
Install one flashing tool such as BLDevCube or blflash.
Build a hello world example from the SDK.
Move the boot jumper to the edge position and press reset.
Flash the program, move the jumper back and press reset again.
Open a serial monitor and read the hello message from the board.
meta: Open Board. From $3.98. A few stores.
